brief.headline: Close a ₹16.09 L gap by matching Mars Plastics prices and pull payment in to 30 days to free ₹10.63 L cash

priceAsk.summary: Match the prices we pay Mars Plastics for the same items
priceAsk.target: Cut ₹16.09 L off our annual bill — bring the 30 ml HDPE bottle down from ₹1.65 to ₹1.38/NOS and the 28 mm PP cap from ₹0.90 to ₹0.81/NOS
priceAsk.basis: Mars Plastics already supplies us identical bottles and caps at those lower prices; we're paying Premier 19.6% more on bottles and 11.1% more on caps for no reason

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.63 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is material enough to matter, but without their numbers we can't gauge how hard to push on price alone. The safest play is to use Mars Plastics as the benchmark — we already pay Mars less, so Premier knows that price exists — and to line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a qualified second source so we're not stuck if Premier won't move.

evidence.point: We pay Premier ₹1.65 per 30 ml HDPE bottle but Mars charges us only ₹1.38 — a 19.6% gap
That one bottle alone costs us an extra ₹11.74 L a year
Premier's 28 mm induction-wad cap is ₹0.90; Mars supplies it at ₹0.81 — an 11.1% gap worth ₹4.23 L yearly
Market asking prices for a 28 mm PP cap with induction wad run ₹0.85–0.95 typical, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — so our Mars price of ₹0.81 is fair and Premier's ₹0.90 is high
Pulling payment in from 45 days to 30 frees ₹10.63 L of our cash
Our total annual spend with Premier is ₹1.29 Cr

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue; makes pharma bottles and caps; health score B (65/100) — the top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100); proven in pharma containers and closures

risks: Premier's financials aren't public — we can't see if they're struggling or stable, so we must rely on our own purchase data and the Mars benchmark to justify the ask
If Premier refuses to match Mars, we risk a supply gap unless Manjushree or Mold-Tek are qualified and ready to quote before we walk
The market-ask verdict says ₹0.85–0.95 is typical for the 28 mm cap, so pushing below ₹0.81 may hit resistance — anchor to the Mars price we already pay, not the lower end of the market band
Faster payment (30 days) is valuable to any supplier, but without knowing Premier's borrowing rate we can't quantify exactly how much — frame it as 'cash certainty' rather than a rate-based swap
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹16.09 lakh more each year than Mars Plastics charges us for the same bottles and caps — let's close that gap and move to 30-day payment so we both get faster, simpler cash flow.
